title: bb_ask: integration (index + embeddings + freshness + read-only)

checks.name: integration: every answer source resolves to an indexed brain_file row
integration: answer is non-empty with provenance and bounds
integration: vector path resolves entities to indexed files
integration: comparison count equals scanned rows when the scan is not capped
integration: vector results carry no NaN similarity [negative]
integration: a semantic answer leaves brain.db and its WAL unchanged [negative]
integration: an aggregate answer leaves brain.db and its WAL unchanged [negative]
integration: a changed file is marked STALE [negative]
checks.detail: --- File: src/beta.ts (Line 1) [MISSING — file no longer on disk] --- | [function] requestHandler — similarity 0.691 [MISSING — file no longer on disk]

checks.name: integration: a deleted file is marked MISSING, not 'changed' [negative]
checks.detail: --- File: src/beta.ts (Line 1) [MISSING — file no longer on disk] --- | [function] requestHandler — similarity 0.691 [MISSING — file no longer on disk]

checks.name: integration: the changed file's result carries stale=true and is not marked missing
integration: the deleted file's result carries missing=true
integration: after refresh the changed file is no longer stale
integration: keyword-fallback path engages with an explicit reason
integration: fallback results resolve to indexed files
integration: fallback results carry no NaN similarity [negative]

decisions.resolution: every cited source resolves to an indexed brain_file row
decisions.freshness: a file changed after indexing is marked STALE; a file deleted after indexing is marked MISSING; the two markers are distinct
decisions.readonly: a semantic answer and an aggregate answer leave brain.db and its WAL byte-identical (0-byte WAL and touched -shm are connection artifacts, not writes)
decisions.refresh: reindexing clears the stale marker — the loop closes

limitations: The lexical-fallback leg's read-only status depends on the shared content-search/symbol-search engines and is asserted in the honesty gate, which names that dependency.
